hook.text: WeChat isn't just messaging. In China, it's payments, taxi rides, medical records, and government ID combined.

buildup.text: Launched in 2011, WeChat now has 1.3 billion users. It's less an app than a digital operating system.

discovery.text: Mini-programs inside WeChat replace standalone apps. You can shop, bank, and date without leaving one app.

twist.text: The government monitors WeChat conversations. Convenience and surveillance are packaged together. No opt-out.

climax.text: Western tech dreams of being WeChat. But WeChat shows the cost: total dependency on a single platform.

punchline.text: WeChat is everything. That's the convenience and the danger.

quiz.question: What makes WeChat a 'super-app'?
options: It combines messaging, payments, services, and government ID
